title: Automated Multi-Cluster Configuration Synchronization
business: Platform engineers managing global Kubernetes fleets across diverse cloud environments.
problem: Manual configuration drift occurs when cluster operators apply changes inconsistently across staging and production environments, leading to environment-specific failures and high operational overhead.
solution: Flux enables declarative delivery by treating Git as the single source of truth, where custom controllers automatically reconcile the cluster state with defined Git repository configurations, ensuring consistency through continuous automated synchronization.
steps: Bootstrap the Flux controllers into the management cluster using the Flux CLI.
Define a GitRepository custom resource to point to the source of truth configuration.
Create a Kustomization resource to specify the target path and synchronization interval for the cluster state.
Configure Kubernetes RBAC to restrict the reconciliation permissions for the specific cluster namespaces.
Monitor the reconciliation health via Flux event notifications sent to external alerting systems.
outcome: A reliable, version-controlled delivery pipeline where cluster state is automatically maintained without manual intervention, significantly reducing configuration drift.
limitation: Flux relies on the Git repository as the source of truth; if the repository becomes unreachable or contains malformed manifests, reconciliation will stall, which can be checked by inspecting the status field of the Kustomization resource.

diagram.title: Flux Reconciliation Flow
diagram.description: The flow shows how Flux bridges Git sources to actual cluster state.

code.content:
apiVersion: source.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1
kind: GitRepository
metadata:
  name: cluster-config
  namespace: flux-system
spec:
  interval: 1m # How often to check for changes
  url: https://github.com/org/repo # Source location
---
apiVersion: kustomize.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1
kind: Kustomization
metadata:
  name: app-sync
  namespace: flux-system
spec:
  path: ./deployments # Path to manifests
  prune: true # Remove resources not in Git
code.explanation: This maps to the scenario by defining the GitRepository source and the Kustomization controller to enforce the desired state defined in the repository.

It replaces Kubernetes RBAC with a proprietary security model.

It is incompatible with Kustomize or Helm configurations.
